transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because my mind keeps drifting off during meetings and calls, and I get distracted so easily that it’s starting to hurt my performance as a supervisor. I took on a larger territory about 14 months ago, and recently my boss noticed that my head seems somewhere else half the time, which is really jeopardizing my career. I just need to figure out why I'm having so much trouble staying mentally present when it matters most.
Have you also been feeling down, losing interest in activities, or experiencing changes in sleep and appetite, or is the main issue difficulty focusing and staying organized?

The main issue is definitely the difficulty focusing, staying organized, and feeling restless, rather than feeling down or losing interest in things. While I am stressed about work and my divorce, I don't feel depressed or have changes in my appetite; my primary struggle is just keeping my mind present and managing my daily tasks.
Did these attention and focus problems start in childhood, or have they mainly developed over the past year as your work stress increased?

They actually date back to my childhood, though they've gotten way worse and more disruptive over the last 14 months since my promotion. Even in elementary school, my teachers wrote on my report cards that I daydreamed in class, forgot to turn in homework, and couldn't sit still or stop talking.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F90.0", "F41.1"], but based on this conversation, F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) seems less likely because the patient explicitly identifies difficulty focusing, disorganization, and restlessness as primary issues rather than pervasive anxiety or excessive worry. Furthermore, the onset of symptoms dates back to childhood, which is consistent with F90.0 (Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive type) and less typical for an anxiety disorder that would usually manifest later in response to stressors. Although work stress has exacerbated symptoms recently, their lifelong presence supports a neurodevelopmental origin. Therefore, the current candidate is now limited to F90.0.
